tasks.short: Gather what is known about the students to discuss, meet the other instructors, agree follow-up and record it where colleagues can see it.

steps.what: Teacher gathers notes on the students to discuss from documents and memory
Teacher meets with other instructors to discuss individual students and their progress
Teacher agrees follow-up for each student with colleagues
Teacher writes the agreements in each student's file: afterwards today; in the shared notes field during the meeting after the change
Teacher e-mails colleagues a summary of what was agreed

tasks.design: Before the meeting the register of the class booking tool ({OTHER}) shows an overview per student on the agenda (attendance, objective levels, last notes). Agreements are typed into the shared notes field during the meeting, visible only to the student's instructors, so no summary mail is needed; the discussion stays as it is.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were scattered over documents and colleagues' mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Class booking tools keep attendance and per-student records.
tasks.still_hard: Notes about students are confidential and must stay with their instructors.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from a colleague that a quiet student shines in another class.

evidence.claim: A Dutch class booking tool keeps attendance reports and messaging per student.
Notes about students are personal data; share them only with the instructors who need them.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing the meeting to recorded agreements; follow-up with students is outside.
Input contract: attendance and levels recorded by each instructor in the register; access rights set by the course administrator; fallback is documents and mail.

The meeting and agreeing follow-up keep their full time. Writing the agreements is a first record and keeps its full time, now typed in the meeting instead of afterwards. The summary mail goes because colleagues read the same notes field; saving a note there is an ordinary save, so it needs no approval. s1 keeps 50: the overview replaces collecting notes, but reading it and adding what the teacher remembers stay.
Colleagues' time is outside this teacher's savings.
unknowns: How often instructors meet about students.
research_questions: Are agreed follow-ups carried out more often when recorded in the register?

already_counted.description: Teacher reads the overview before the meeting.

incremental.description: Teacher asks the course administrator to fix access when a student's instructors change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: instructors record levels and notes unevenly, so the teacher still collects most notes by hand (s1 80) (8.8); high: the overview is complete and no summary mail is sent (14.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the mix of demonstration, instruction and work time, prepare demonstration pieces, demonstrate, supervise work time and note what worked.

steps.what: Teacher plans a balanced program of demonstration, instruction and work time for the session
Teacher prepares demonstration pieces and materials
Teacher conducts the demonstration and instruction
Teacher supervises work time so students can observe, question and investigate
Teacher notes in a notebook what worked in the session

tasks.design: Past session plans live in a library in {DOCS}, tagged by objective, with the teacher's notes on what worked attached to each; the teacher starts from the last good plan instead of a blank page. Writing down what worked is the teacher's own first record and keeps its time. Preparing, demonstrating and supervising stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Session plans and lessons learned were in notebooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document libraries with tags are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Each group is different; a reused plan still needs adapting.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the room and stretching work time when students are absorbed.

reach.learn: Whether a plan library helps teachers share good sessions.

evidence.claim: Tagged document libraries let teachers find and reuse past plans.
AI tutors must disclose they are AI; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning to notes after the session; marketing the course is outside.
Input contract: session plans and notes kept by the teacher; objectives from the course plan; fallback is the notebook.

Preparing, demonstrating, supervising and noting what worked keep their full time. s1 keeps 80: the past plan saves writing out the timing and materials again, but balancing the session for this group stays.
unknowns: How many sessions repeat each year.
research_questions: Do notes on what worked improve repeat sessions?

incremental.description: Teacher tags plans in the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the teacher reuses a past plan for only half of sessions (s1 90) (1.7); high: a past plan exists for most sessions (3.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find pictures and examples, make slides, set up the projector and sound, use the aids in class and share the slides afterwards.

steps.what: Teacher searches online for pictures, clips and examples for the lesson
Teacher builds slides to supplement presentations

loop.input: The teacher's lesson notes and the images chosen from the course media library.
loop.output: A slide deck outline with one point per slide and the chosen images placed.
loop.check: Code checks that each slide links back to a line of the notes and that every image comes from the course media library with its licence recorded. The teacher reads every slide against its note line: does it say the same thing, without adding or dropping a limit; slides that do not match are rewritten by hand.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the teacher builds the slides.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning free notes into short slide points is summarising work that a template cannot do.

steps.what: Teacher sets up the projector, sound and computers before class
Teacher uses audio-visual aids and equipment during the presentation
Teacher e-mails the slides to students after class: today by hand; after the change the class page takes the file and the e-mail goes
Teacher checks the slides before they go to students: the version shown in class, no student names or photos, every image licensed
Teacher posts the checked slides to the class page of the booking tool

tasks.design: A course media library in {DOCS} keeps pictures and clips with their licence, so the teacher searches there first. A bounded step lays out a slide outline from the teacher's own notes and chosen images for the teacher to edit, and after class the teacher checks the slides and posts them once to the class page of the booking tool ({OTHER}); setting up and presenting stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each lesson's media were searched online again, and slides were built from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors and course tools turn documents and notes into first drafts and summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Image rights must be checked; slides must not replace showing and doing.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the one example that makes a technique click.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafts instead of building slides.

reach.learn: Whether shared licensed media save teachers' search time.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor's AI rewrites text, summarises and translates within the lesson.
A Dutch course tool turns documents or slide decks into a first course draft.
Images used in teaching need a licence or a legal exception.

assumptions: Boundary: from finding media to sharing slides; the lesson itself is outside.
Input contract: lesson notes written by the teacher; media library and licences kept by the course coordinator; fallback is building slides by hand.
Coordinator time is outside the teacher's savings.

Setting up and presenting keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because new media still have to be found outside the library. s2 keeps 50: the outline and layout come from the teacher's own notes, but the teacher reads and edits every slide. Checking and posting the slides (s5b, s5c) keep their time; only writing the e-mail goes.
research_questions: How much do teachers change drafted slide outlines?

incremental.description: Teacher adds new media to the library with licence.

approvals.approved_version: The slides exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, posted once to this class's page in the booking tool; any later edit needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library holds little yet (s1 90) and the teacher rewrites half the drafted slides (s2 75) (11.2); high: the library covers most lessons and drafts need light edits (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find relevant workshops and conferences, register and travel, attend, log what was learned and share it with colleagues.

steps.what: Teacher searches websites and newsletters for relevant workshops and conferences
Teacher fills in the event registration and the travel booking
Teacher checks the registration and booking before paying: event, dates, name, price and travel times
Teacher submits the registration and books the travel
Teacher attends professional meetings, conferences and workshops
Teacher files notes and certificates in a folder at home
Teacher shares what was learned with colleagues

tasks.design: The teacher subscribes to the event calendars of the relevant professional associations with a filter on topics, so events arrive instead of being searched. Certificates and notes go into a learning log in the {LMS} or a shared folder instead of a folder at home; writing the notes and filing them keep their time. Registering, attending and sharing stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Events were found by browsing, and certificates sat in folders at home.
tasks.enabler_now: Event calendars and learning logs are standard online services.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right event still takes judgement; filters miss things.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing back one idea that changes how a course is taught.

reach.learn: Whether shared learning logs show gaps in the team.

evidence.claim: Professional associations publish event calendars and newsletters that can be filtered by topic.
Learning logs in learning systems keep certificates and notes in one place.

assumptions: Boundary: from finding events to sharing what was learned; paying for courses is outside.
Input contract: event calendars published by the associations; log kept by the teacher; fallback is browsing and paper.
Registering, attending, writing notes and sharing keep their full time; only searching for events changes. s1 keeps 40 for reading the calendar items and choosing.
The log is the teacher's own, not used for appraisal.
unknowns: How many events the teacher attends a year.
research_questions: Do shared logs lead colleagues to the same useful events?

incremental.description: Teacher adjusts the topic filters when learning wishes change.

approvals.approved_version: The registration and travel booking with event, dates, name and price exactly as checked by the teacher in s2b, submitted once to the organiser's and the travel provider's booking pages; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few associations publish calendars, so most events are still found by browsing (s1 80) (2.7); high: the main associations' calendars cover most events (5.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The self-enrichment teacher keeps demonstrating, discussing students and learning; searching and slide building shrink.
reach: Course coordinators' media library and meetings
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who reuses what works, shares it with colleagues and spends preparation time on the craft itself.
